lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Label the code-profile URL or use a recognizable domain.
items.because: Recruiters should immediately know whether it is GitHub, a personal site, or a portfolio.

items.says: Add LinkedIn only if it is complete and consistent with the resume.
Add links to the package, working paper, or publications where appropriate.
items.because: Readers should not have to search for them.

items.says: Use the university’s official degree name and indicate candidacy only if you have formally advanced to candidacy.
items.because: 'Ph.D. candidate' has a specific institutional meaning.

items.says: Use consistent date punctuation throughout the document; en dashes are cleaner than spaced hyphens.
Consider adding your dissertation area, adviser, or expected dissertation title if it directly supports quantitative-finance applications.
Add GPA only if it is strong and useful.
items.because: At the Ph.D. level, research is generally more important.

items.says: Add honors or GPA only if notably strong.
Confirm whether the one-year period between the B.S. and Ph.D. was entirely covered by the research-assistant role.
items.because: A reader may wonder whether you were employed by the university or enrolled in another program.

items.says: If confidentiality permits, identify the asset-class or desk context more precisely.
items.because: The bullets imply futures-focused systematic research, but the scope is not fully clear.

items.says: Make sure all performance numbers and claims have been approved for external use by the employer.
Qualify the attribution behind the Sharpe increase.
items.because: Claiming that one signal raised the entire desk book’s Sharpe from 1.1 to 1.5 can sound implausibly causal unless this was measured in a controlled portfolio comparison.

items.says: Specify whether the Sharpe figures are annualized and whether they refer to the signal, a strategy sleeve, or the full desk portfolio.
Consider reducing precision or adding statistical context because 18 months is a relatively short evaluation window for a Sharpe estimate.
Define the turnover convention if space allows.
items.because: 'Daily turnover' can be calculated several ways.

items.says: Clarify whether the slippage reduction was modeled, simulated, or observed.
items.because: The methodology should be defensible in an interview.

items.says: Verify that 'keeping 90% of gross returns' is directly comparable before and after smoothing and over the same test period.
This bullet may partially overlap with the first bullet.
items.because: Keep it only if transaction-cost engineering is important to the target role.

items.says: Replace the explanatory ending with a more concrete validation outcome if one exists.
items.because: The current ending explains what proper backtesting means rather than showing what the validation established.

items.says: Clarify how the six years of data relate to the 18-month out-of-sample period in the first bullet.
items.because: A reviewer may otherwise see an inconsistency.

items.says: Add the principal technologies if they are not captured elsewhere, particularly SQL, data-storage tools, orchestration tools, or distributed-computing systems.
Quantify scale or efficiency if available: instruments, records, storage volume, compute-time reduction, or researcher-hours saved.
Ensure 'feature store' is technically accurate rather than a general feature-generation library.
State whether the allocation was actually launched if you know that it was.
items.because: Approval for a future allocation is weaker than deployment.

items.says: Avoid disclosing allocation size or proprietary capacity details unless explicitly permitted.
Add the date or status only if the allocation remained pending when the internship ended.
Consider removing this bullet first if you need space.
items.because: This is credible but lower-value than the research, validation, infrastructure, and allocation bullets.

items.says: The onboarding claim may be difficult to verify because it occurred after your internship.
items.because: Retain it only if someone at the firm directly confirmed that outcome.

items.says: If kept, focus on the durable research process rather than routine wiki documentation.
Clarify whether this was a full-time staff research-assistant position, a post-baccalaureate appointment, or part of another program.
items.because: The dates precede the Ph.D. and may prompt questions.

items.says: If teaching was a separate appointment, do not place it under the research-assistant title; split it into a separate teaching-assistant role.
Add the cluster or parallel-computing technologies used if relevant to the jobs you are targeting.
Clarify whether the reduction reflects parallelization, algorithmic improvements, caching, or all three.
Remove the reference to 'Section 3.'
items.because: A section number is an internal manuscript detail and does not establish your contribution clearly.

items.says: Clarify your authorship position and whether you personally proved the result or contributed jointly.
Give the manuscript title elsewhere or add a publications/research section if the paper is substantial.
Confirm the journal status precisely. 'Under review' should mean formally submitted and currently in review, not planned for submission.
Move this to a distinct teaching role if teaching was not part of the research-assistant appointment.
Clarify whether you created all 12 problem sets or contributed to them.
Add response rate or number of evaluations if the 4.8/5 rating came from a small subset of students.
This can be shortened or removed if space is limited.
items.because: It is less relevant than research for most quant roles.

items.says: Add the package name and a direct repository or package-registry link.
Specify your ownership level if it was collaborative.
Define the download source and measurement window so the 3,000 figure is credible.
Add a link to the paper or repository if public.
Indicate a current milestone or status for the ongoing project.
items.because: A long-running 'present' project without a recent deliverable can appear stale.

items.says: If this is dissertation-related rather than independent, label it accurately.
Consider naming key data sources if they are public and recognizable.
Specify the exact evaluation design: forecast horizon, test period, and whether the 7% is an average across indices or an aggregate loss reduction.
Clarify whether the model comparison used identical information sets and tuning budgets.
Consider adding at least one stronger benchmark if HAR-RV was the only baseline.
items.because: Otherwise the result may appear benchmark-dependent.

items.says: Define the two crisis periods; the current phrase assumes knowledge the reader does not have.
Verify that the Diebold–Mariano procedure accounts appropriately for forecast overlap and serial dependence.
Clarify whether Holm correction was applied across all 30 index-level tests.
Avoid implying that significance in 24 indices proves broad economic value; statistical and economic significance should remain distinct.
Preserve the result while reducing methodological detail if space becomes constrained.
items.because: This bullet is technically strong but dense.

items.says: Include the paper title and link rather than emphasizing page count.
items.because: Length is not a meaningful quality indicator.

items.says: Clarify whether the seminar presentation was invited, selected, or part of a routine internal series.
State whether you presented it personally.
Consider separating the paper into a 'Research' or 'Publications and Presentations' section if you have multiple scholarly outputs.
Use the actual competition name rather than a generic description.
Add the competition link and your team or profile link if public.
The rank and top-percentile statement are redundant. Keep the more precise ranking measure or the percentile, not both.
Clarify your individual contribution rather than presenting the full team result as solely yours.
State whether the placement was on the final private leaderboard, as currently implied, and ensure the competition rules permitted the approach.
Reconsider the phrase 'cut validation leakage.'
items.because: It can suggest that earlier modeling decisions were made using contaminated validation.

items.says: Identify the leakage mechanism more precisely: temporal mixing, group overlap, target leakage, or another issue.
Explain whether the corrected validation scheme was adopted before final model selection.
The 0.02 gap needs a named metric; without one, the magnitude is not interpretable.
Be cautious about treating agreement with the leaderboard as proof of a valid model-selection process.
Specify your personal ownership clearly, particularly because this was a team project.
Confirm that permutation importance and feature selection were calculated within the training or cross-validation process rather than on a repeatedly reused holdout set.
Replace feature-count reduction with runtime, memory, stability, or interpretability gains if those were measured; reducing feature count without score loss is useful but incomplete.
Keep the no-performance-loss outcome if it was measured on an untouched validation set.
Separate programming languages from libraries/frameworks. Python and R are languages; PyTorch is a framework.
Add SQL, Git, Linux, shell scripting, cloud tools, cluster schedulers, and relevant data technologies if you can use them competently.
Include C++ only if you can discuss and code in it under interview conditions.
Add core Python libraries selectively if they strengthen keyword matching, especially NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, and statsmodels.
Avoid proficiency ratings unless an application explicitly asks for them.

Expand this to include the strongest methods already demonstrated in the resume: market microstructure, backtesting, transaction-cost modeling, volatility forecasting, Monte Carlo methods, and statistical inference.
Do not list methods merely for keyword coverage; expect technical questions on every item.
Keep terminology consistent with the experience bullets. For example, the resume currently demonstrates more finance-specific expertise than the skills section communicates.
Use one consistent date format and one dash style throughout.
Keep bullets to roughly one or two lines where possible; several currently wrap to three lines.
Consider limiting Northpeak to four or five bullets and the research role to three or four.
items.because: The strongest Northpeak bullets are the signal result, cost reduction, validation, feature infrastructure, and live-allocation decision.

items.says: Add a Research/Publications section if the JASA manuscript and volatility paper are both substantive and public.
items.because: That would make your academic record easier to assess.

items.says: Maintain reverse chronological order.
Keep the resume to one page for most internship or early-career quant applications unless publications require a second page.
Ensure every numerical claim is explainable, reproducible, and permissible to disclose.
items.because: Quant interviewers are likely to probe the Sharpe, turnover, slippage, significance tests, leakage controls, and tighter-bound claims closely.
